key_insight: The paper shows that IQP quantum kernels have a finite, bandwidth-controlled Fourier structure in their RKHS, leading to distinct localized, multimodal, or periodic expressivity regimes.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical rule for tuning quantum kernel bandwidth to match the data’s structure, improving model selection for classification and anomaly detection.
method: Derived an RKHS Fourier representation for IQP feature maps.
Characterized accessible frequencies from circuit design and bandwidth scaling.
Tested the theory on synthetic datasets and compared against a Gaussian kernel.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic datasets with controlled periodic and multimodal structure reproduced the predicted regimes across dimensions and feature-map settings in both supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection.
watch_item: The expressivity gains are data-dependent, so mismatched bandwidth or unsupported data structure may limit practical benefit.
paper_title: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
